answer: Retrospective Correlation Scoring. After the fact, the system clusters new identities by shared behavioral fingerprints: synchronized timing, identical transaction graphs, reused infrastructure. When a cluster exceeds a threshold of correlated accounts, every member is demoted below the reef of trusted reputation, losing access to high-value actions. Each identity must therefore sustain distinct, plausible behavior for weeks before gaining standing—a jetty of effort per account an attacker cannot cheaply mass-produce. The ocean of marginal accounts becomes expensive to fake,
